newsitem.title: USA: Voters in Hawaii OK bonds for hurricane insurance.
newsitem.headline: Voters in Hawaii OK bonds for hurricane insurance.

text.p: Voters in Hawaii have approved a measure that will allow the state to issue up to $500 million of revenue bonds to help stabilize insurance rates, state officials said on Wednesday.

Constitutional Amendment One, approved by 64 percent of state voters, will allow the state to issue $500 million in revenue bond for the Hawaii Hurricane Relief Fund, which issues policies covering hurricane risk.
State officials said the bond issue would reduce the need to purchase reinsurance coverage, currently costing the fund $80 million annually.

Proponents said the bonds, which could be issued before or after a major hurricane, would allow the Hawaii Hurricane Relief Fund to reduce reinsurance costs and accumulate premiums. The bonds could also be used to augment the fund's ability to pay claims, proponents said.

Opponents of the measure said the use of revenue bonds to create a pool of funds for insurance purposes was not a generally accepted practice. They warned that the feasibility of marketing these revenue bonds was doubtful since the revenue base to support the bonds could be at risk in the event of a hurricane catastrophe.

Voters also approved a measure that will allow the state to appropriate the funds of the state educational facilities improvement special fund for period beyond three years to allow for acquisition and construction of public school facilities.
